annotationRationale: Logarithm rules reduce the hypothesis to a bounded integer equation. The alternative uses a genuinely different restriction through square residues modulo 5.

classificationReview.areaRationale: The main work transforms logarithmic expressions into algebraic equations with integer restrictions, so Algebra replaces Unclassified.
classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is an appropriate repair: logarithmic transformations drive the reduction, followed by elementary integer restrictions.

review.questionCheck: Writing the square-root terms as positive integers p and q forces both to be even. The resulting equation m(m+1)+n(n+1)=50 has only {m,n}={4,5}, giving ab=10^164, choice D. The printed conditions, choices, and key are consistent.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Neither source collection supplies sharedQuestions. LIVE Q15 and Random Math Q15's first method are retained in bounded-integer-search. The existing square-completion and modular routes are combined in odd-squares-modulo-five. Random Math's second, answer-choice-based square search is reasonably omitted because it repeats finite enumeration with additional dependence on the choices.
review.annotationCheck: Logarithm properties and complete integer-equation solving are appropriate assessed concepts, with the logarithm definition supporting conversion back to ab. Square completion and congruences are correctly identified on the alternative route.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is an appropriate repair: logarithmic transformations drive the reduction, followed by elementary integer restrictions.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Integrality of p²/2 and q²/2 correctly forces even p and q. Positivity and 7·8>50 bound m,n to 1 through 6. The table is complete, only 20+30=50 works, and the reconstructed terms 8,10,32,50 verify the original condition.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: This accurately reconstructs the even-integer substitution and bounded search in LIVE Q15 and Random Math Q15's first solution. Both third-party references are credited under the correct source-informed-original basis; the prose is independently explanatory.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why integrality matters. Parity, the finite bound, the table entries, uniqueness, and logarithmic recovery of the answer are sufficiently justified.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The logarithm definition, logarithm rules, and integer-equation synthesis nodes precisely cover the derivation and completeness argument.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native logarithm-definition and operation links fit. The bounded integer-equation argument has no supplied accepted CN alignment.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: Optional F-BF.B.5 supports the logarithm and exponent relationship used here. F-LE.A.4 has only conceptual overlap because no exponential model or technological evaluation is involved. The integer search has no supplied US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All immediate nodes are supported, and the finite table establishes the completeness required by integer-diophantine-equations.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Square completion correctly gives u²+v²=202 with odd u,v≥3, hence u,v∈{3,5,7,9,11,13}. Square residues modulo 5 force both residues to be 1, leaving only 9 and 11. Only their mixed pair sums to 202, giving p,q=8,10 and ab=10^164.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The references supply the logarithmic substitution, while the square-completion and modulo-5 continuation is accurately identified as original development incorporating the existing route. Both references are credited without claiming official authorship.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The finite domain and square residues are explained at use. Repeated choices are checked explicitly, so the modular restriction and final uniqueness are reconstructible without an unexplained number-theory fact.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The logarithm, square-completion, congruence, and integer-equation nodes all correspond to substantive written steps.
